title.narrative: Integrated Urban Services and Resilience Improvement Project

description.narrative: The project will strengthen the resilience of the population and ecosystem in Majuro and Ebeye through improved urban services, which will help households better withstand and adapt to climate change impacts and disaster risks, including extended drought, storm surge, and sea level rise. The project will enhance the water security of Majuro communities through the provision of continuous, resilient, and potable piped water supply services.

Sustainability, circularity, and climate and disaster resilience of urban services in the Marshall Islands improved.

At least 70% of households or about 16,000 people living in Majuro (including at least 70% of women-headed households) have 24/7 access to safe, resilient, and affordable water supply. Progress/Status: The Water Treatment Facility component is being revised to manage cost overruns and implementation risks while maintaining the objective of 24-hour water service. The package includes rehabilitation of WTP-C and WTP-A, expansion of the Hospital RO plant, relocation of the MIHS RO plant, and installation of pressure tanks to support a gradual transition to continuous water supply. Works are expected to start in Q4 2026. Data Source: Water production records, operational data, project performance management reports by Majuro Water and Sewer Company (MWSC) Actual value:

Nonrevenue water in Majuro reduced to 25%. Progress/Status: The initial procurement of the pipeline relining works was unsuccessful, with the only bid received being nonresponsive and nearly four times the available budget. The pipe relining component is being reassessed through a comprehensive pipeline condition assessment, including CCTV inspection, leak detection, and mapping, to identify and prioritize critical rehabilitation needs. Based on the finding, targeted relining package(s) will be rebid, while alternative solutions, including a new transmission main, will continue to be explored. The assessment work is expected to start in Q4 2026. Data Source: Water production records, operational data, project performance management reports by Majuro Water and Sewer Company (MWSC) Actual value:

At least 35% of generated waste in Majuro reduced, recovered, or recycled, and diverted from landfill site. Progress/Status: The pilot landfill rehabilitation works under the PRF informed the design of the full-scale Rairok landfill improvement and rehabilitation works. The detailed engineering design and draft bidding documents are being finalizied. Bidding is expected to commence in Q3 2026. Data Source: Operational data, project performance management reports by Majuro Atoll Waste Company (MAWC) Actual value:
